metaData.title: A Comprehensive Guide to Meta's 2026 Shareholder Meeting: Zuckerberg Bets Big on Four AI Directions, All Ten Shareholder Proposals Rejected
metaData.oneSentenceSummary: Meta's 2026 annual shareholder meeting rejected all ten shareholder proposals, while Zuckerberg outlined four key AI strategic directions and announced the global launch of subscription services.
metaData.summary: This article provides a detailed report on the core content of Meta's 2026 annual shareholder meeting. The meeting rejected all ten shareholder proposals, including those on AI data usage risk reports, abolishing the dual-class share structure, and child safety, with the highest support rate reaching only 27%. During the meeting, Zuckerberg elaborated on four directions of the AI strategy: using AI to improve core applications and advertising, personal AI agents, business agents, and AI hardware. He projected capital expenditures of $115-135 billion for 2026, nearly double the previous year's figure. Following the meeting, Meta announced the global launch of subscription services for consumers and AI users, including Instagram Plus, Facebook Plus, WhatsApp Plus, and the Meta One series for AI users. The article also covers topics such as board elections, executive compensation, the prospects of Reality Labs, and capital returns.

mainPoints.point: Meta's 2026 annual shareholder meeting rejected all ten shareholder proposals.
mainPoints.explanation: Proposals covering issues such as AI data usage risks, abolishing the dual-class share structure, child safety, and climate change commitments were all rejected, with the highest support rate reaching only 27%, reflecting Zuckerberg's absolute control over the company.

mainPoints.point: Zuckerberg divided the AI strategy into four directions: core applications and advertising, personal AI agents, business agents, and AI hardware.
mainPoints.explanation: AI has improved ranking recommendations and ad targeting; personal AI agents will offer both free and paid versions; business agent conversations have grown tenfold; daily active users of AI glasses have doubled year-over-year, making it one of the fastest-growing consumer electronics categories.

mainPoints.point: Meta announced the global launch of subscription services to explore AI monetization models.
mainPoints.explanation: For consumers, Meta launched Instagram Plus, Facebook Plus, and WhatsApp Plus (priced at $2.99-$3.99 per month); for AI users, it launched the Meta One series ($7.99-$19.99 per month), offering greater computing power and more features.

mainPoints.point: Meta's 2026 capital expenditure is projected at $115-135 billion, nearly doubling.
mainPoints.explanation: Most of the investment is directed toward AI infrastructure, but Zuckerberg acknowledged that AI revenue has not yet fully materialized. The company is still in a phase of heavy investment, following a model of building products first, confirming retention, and then monetizing.

keyQuotes: This is the most exciting time I've seen in our industry in the 20 years I've been running this company.
I hear a lot of people say that AI will replace humans, but I believe AI will actually amplify people's ability to do what they want to do.

For the first time in Meta's history, we will be able to not just observe statistical patterns, but build a principled understanding of what you care about and the actual content of each piece of content.
The company's top priority right now is to invest resources to position itself as a leader in the AI field.

relatedArticles.title: Why Did Hermes Take Over from OpenClaw in Just Two Months?
relatedArticles.oneSentenceSummary: This article provides an in-depth comparison between the rising open-source AI Agent star Hermes and its predecessor OpenClaw, arguing that Hermes' success stems not from functional superiority but from encapsulating decision complexity—such as skill auto-evolution and proactive memory management—within underlying deterministic rules. This engineering safety net allowed it to deliver an automated 'gets better with use' experience precisely when the underlying technology was just barely sufficient.
